title: A CITY BUILT INSIDE A SLEEPING SONG
deck: The city of Aubade is made of a sleeper's slow music, and the sleeper has begun to wake. Its engineers mean to cut the rhythm at the seventh bell; its choirs have noticed that every rest ends on a note someone else sings. Illuminara has one long evening to learn what the sleeper is asking, and what the city is willing to give to hear it.
shape: Six scenes across one afternoon and night: a cutting set for the seventh bell; a phrase with no fourth note; a square that votes and a copy that rings flat and costs a street; a question asked by leaving it open; a kitchen conversation in which one room is crossed on trust before any street is; and a waking in which some leave, some stay, and the count is said aloud.

scenes.title: The Third Rest
paragraphs: *Aubade, the Stair of Bells - The third rest of the day, 14:10*

The paving of the Stair hummed under Illuminara's boots, a low even note she felt in the roots of her teeth, and every few steps the hum thinned and came back, the way a breath thins in the moment before someone decides to let it go.
She had come in through the edge of the city an hour ago, summoned by forty-two sung notes whose plain meaning she had read as a hand held out: *please, anyone who can hold things up.*

Now the flight above her sagged, pale tuned stone going soft at the middle like a candle in a warm room, and a woman with a market basket stopped on the step with her mouth open and did not scream, which Illuminara noticed and respected. She set her palms flat against the air in front of the stair. The weight came onto her arms like a wet tent. She breathed out, and the stone stood up into its note again.

At the top a bronze fork stood in a paved court, taller than any church: the Metronome. Under its root a man in ink-black cuffs knelt over a wedge of cold iron the size of a door, and he did not look up until she was standing over him.

**Hale Ostrov** 
You are the one Marrow sang for. I told her not to.

**Illuminara** 
She said you would let me in anyway.

**Hale Ostrov** 
I let in anyone who can carry weight. I watched you carry some. Can you carry all of it?

**Illuminara** 
No. Not all, and not for long. What is the wedge for?

**Hale Ostrov** 
The rests are getting longer. Twenty minutes this morning, fifty now. Near the seventh bell there will be one long enough to leave the Metronome bare to its root, and I will drive this in and lock the rhythm. The rests stop. The city goes on being a city.

**Illuminara** 
And the one whose rhythm it is?

**Hale Ostrov** 
Sleeps.
He said it without flinching.

**Illuminara** 
Could people walk out, during a rest? Out through the edge, the way I came?

**Hale Ostrov** 
The ones who live near it do. Nine thousand, ten. The rest live too deep; the edge has shut again before they reach it. Two hundred thousand people, Illuminara. Tell me where they stand if I am not allowed to cut. Tell me where ethics keeps them.
She did not answer, because she did not have an answer yet, and he had earned a true silence rather than a quick one. Under their feet the paving thinned and came back.
Ilse Marrow came up the Stair with her choir behind her, a broad woman in a scarf of ten colours of wool.

**Ilse Marrow** 
Hale. You've not driven it yet.

**Hale Ostrov** 
The seventh bell, Ilse. You know that.

**Ilse Marrow** 
I know you say it like a man reading his own name off a stone.
She turned to Illuminara and did not waste a breath on greeting.

**Ilse Marrow** 
I tune the choirs of Low Cadence. I'm the one who sang. At the end of every rest we settle the city, and nine times now we've settled it and nine times it has stood. Before anyone puts iron in anything, I want you to listen to what we settle.

**Illuminara** 
There is nothing I would rather do.
Over the court the hum dropped by a half-step, as it did, Ilse said, when a rest was nearly done. Illuminara turned to listen.

scenes.title: The Phrase With No Fourth Note
paragraphs: *The foot of the Stair, among the choir - 14:52*

She had expected a voice, a sentence, something she could set against what Hale wanted. What came first was warmth: a pressure on the back of her neck, like a hand resting there to see whether she would flinch. Then the phrase.

Three notes, each higher than the last, each held a little longer, the way a child holds a banister at the top of a stair it is not sure it wants to climb. After the third there was a stop. It was not silence. Silence is the absence of a note. This had the shape of a note with the note taken out, like the hollow in a pillow where a head has been.

She listened to it five times without moving. The sixth time she noticed what she had been hearing without hearing it: the stop was not where the singer had run out of breath. It was where the singer was waiting.

**Illuminara** 
It isn't unfinished. It's asking.

**Ilse Marrow** 
Asking what?

**Illuminara** 
I don't know yet. But it leaves a place for the answer, every time, exactly the same size.
Ilse stared at her. Then something went across her broad face that was not quite understanding yet, only the shadow understanding throws first.

**Ilse Marrow** 
Oh. Oh, that's the Closing. That's the note we give it.

The Closing was one long falling note, which every child in Aubade learned before it learned to read, sung at curfew and at the end of every rest the way other cities ring a bell. The choir drew up in rows on the wide steps, and Ilse raised one hand.

It was the most beautiful thing Illuminara had heard in the city: fifty voices going down a staircase of a single note, so gently that the stone under them seemed to lie down. And she felt what the Sleeper did when it arrived. The warm hand at her neck closed. It did not close like a fist. It closed like the hand of someone very tired who has been told, kindly, that it may stop. The hum steadied. The Stair stiffened into its ordinary self, polished and cold. The rest was over.
It had finished its sentence in someone else's voice, and gone back under it.

**Ilse Marrow** 
You heard something.

**Illuminara** 
I heard it once, so I may be wrong. I'll tell you what I heard and you tell me where it's false. The phrase has three notes and a gap. The gap is the same every time. You fill it with a falling note. And when you do, it goes down.

**Ilse Marrow** 
Three hundred years we've sung it, every night, because it was the song. You are telling me we put it to sleep.

**Illuminara** 
I'm telling you that you have sung to it for three hundred years because you love it, and that the song also closes a door. I think both are true. I don't think one cancels the other.

**Ilse Marrow** 
If we don't sing it, the rests run long. And the city comes apart.

**Illuminara** 
Parts of it might. I can hold some while people walk out. Not all, and not for long. But the other way is to close the door for good, and nobody ever finds out what it was waiting for.

**Ilse Marrow** 
I'm not deciding this for two hundred thousand people alone. And I'm not doing it behind Hale's back. I'll put it to the square at the sixth bell, to his face. If the square says sing, I sing, and you hold your tongue.

**Illuminara** 
I will.

**Ilse Marrow** 
Good. I'd have thought less of you if you'd said anything else.

scenes.title: The Square, and the Copy That Rang Flat
paragraphs: *The Metronome court - The sixth bell, 18:00, and after*
The square filled the court and the steps below it, ten thousand lamps held at shoulder height, and the argument went the way arguments go when the thing argued about is under everybody's feet.

**Anselm Duret** 
Five rests, Ilse. Six. My models say the lower arcades go first, and the Lower Arcade is where I keep my shop and my sister keeps hers. You want to vote my street off the map so a mountain can have a different bedtime?

**Ilse Marrow** 
I want to vote to hear what the mountain says. I want to leave it the place and see if it answers. That is all I am asking you to do.

A woman near the back, Nel Vasco, said she had sung the Closing to her dying son and would not hear it called a cage. Then, in a smaller voice, she said she would like to know. Hale Ostrov listened to all of it and said nothing. Illuminara stood with her hands folded and her tongue kept, which was harder than the stair had been, and when the lamps went up she did not look to see how many.

They went up for an hour and a quarter, and then they stayed up. It was not a large majority. A man near the front had lifted his lamp and then lowered it with visible shame, and his wife had taken his wrist and lifted it again.
Now, with the Metronome bare to its root and the first thinning already in the stones, Hale spoke without turning.

**Hale Ostrov** 
I will not drive the iron until I have shown you why the other road fails. My guild has built a field of glass bells on the plain beyond the Sleeper's brow, three hundred of them, tuned to the city's keys. I will copy the lowest flight of the Stair into it. If it works, I will wait. If it fails, you will stand aside.

**Illuminara** 
Have you asked it? The one whose steps they are.

**Hale Ostrov** 
Asked the floor if I may take a piece of the floor? In what language? I have six rests before my models say the lower arcades go. A flight of steps is cheap. I am taking the small thing first.

**Illuminara** 
I don't know. I'd like to try, before you take.

She thought of saying no. She had the strength to stop him, and she felt the weight of that, and set it down the way you put back a coin you do not mean to spend. A flight of steps was not a life. Had it been, she would have stopped him, and she knew how thin the margin was. The city was his, and Ilse's, and the Sleeper's. It was not hers to decide.

The rest came on. The hum dropped, and the court floor went from stone to something warm and soft and dark. Hale struck the master chime. Far below, on the plain, one glass bell rang flat, a quarter-tone under where it should have been: the sound of something taken without being offered.

Then the Sleeper flinched. It was not a roar. A roar would have been an answer. It was a clench, the whole warm dark of the court closing like a fist, and every stone in Aubade shuddered once. Down at the Lower Arcade, a street of ropewalks and chandlers with ninety rooms above them, the ground went out from under the ground floor.

Illuminara did not so much run as arrive. Her palms met the air in front of the arcade's falling face and the weight of ninety rooms came onto her arms, an avalanche, slowed. She felt her knees take it.

**Illuminara** 
Walk. Don't run. Take the stair on the left.

Three hundred people walked, with coats and cats and rolled mattresses, an old woman carrying a canary in a scarf, two boys carrying a third. A man went down last but one with a set of brass scales in his arms. She stood there until the last of them had gone, and she counted. Then she let go, and ninety rooms stopped being rooms.

**Anselm Duret** 
I voted to keep singing. It's my street that went.

**Ilse Marrow** 
It went because we took, Anselm. Not because we asked.

**Anselm Duret** 
Does that make the roof any better?

**Illuminara** 
No.

When she came back up the Stair, Hale was standing in the court with the iron at his feet. He did not look like a man who had been proved right. He looked like a man who had been proved right at a price.

**Illuminara** 
Give me this rest. The choir will not sing. It will run long, and it will not close behind me. Give me until it ends.
He looked at the iron, at the bare root of the fork, at the tear in the city below. When he answered, he answered the stone and not her.

**Hale Ostrov** 
Until it ends. The wedge stays in my hand.

scenes.title: Asking
paragraphs: *Inside the rest, under the Metronome - 19:40*

To go to the Sleeper she did the simplest thing, which was to stop being anywhere else. She knelt at the root of the great fork and laid her palm on the court, and the court was no longer a floor. It was warm, and it gave a little, and it smelled of copper and of rain on slate. Somewhere in it a pulse ran, slower than any heart she knew: one beat in the time it takes to walk across the court.
She hummed three notes, each higher than the last, each held a little longer. Then she stopped, and held the stop.

She did not sing the fourth. Everything in her wanted to; it is the most natural thing in the world to fill a place that has been left for you. She felt the wanting rise in her throat like a laugh in church, and she let it stand there and did not use it. *I will not finish it for you.* She said it inwardly, over and over, as one says a name to a sleeper to bring them up slowly.
The silence went on. Overhead the Metronome rang once, very faintly, as a glass does when a finger passes near it. Her knees began to ache. A long way off, a child was being told to hush.
And the Sleeper sang the fourth note.

It was not the Closing. The Closing fell. This rose: a note higher than the third, bright and slightly wrong and entirely its own, and when it sounded every bell in the city rang with it at once, the three hundred glass bells on the plain and the iron in Hale's hand and the stairs themselves, all of Aubade struck like a glass and singing. Illuminara, who had braced for everything but this, laughed out loud. It was a short, helpless, delighted sound, the laugh of someone who has heard a thing finish its own sentence for the first time.

What reached her next was not speech. It was an arrangement of warmth and pressure that she turned into words the way you turn the weather into a decision about a coat. She said aloud each time that she was guessing, and each time the warmth leaned in to correct her.

**The Sleeper** 
Someone stopped asking.

**Illuminara** 
Yes. Three hundred years ago. And then they thought you were weather.

**The Sleeper** 
I was singing. Then it was finished. Then I was the floor.

**Illuminara** 
I know. I'm sorry it took so long for someone to leave you the place.

**The Sleeper** 
They are warm. I hear them in the rests. I do not want them cold. I want my thought back.

**Illuminara** 
They can't all stay in it when you wake. Part of the city is your thought.

**The Sleeper** 
I know which is me and which is them. I can feel the edge. I can lend a rest. A rest lent is a rest I do not wake in.
She understood then what she was being offered, and what it would cost the one offering. She asked it the only way she could think to, plainly, and without pressing.

**Illuminara** 
There is a field of glass bells beside you. If you lend your attention, a district at a time, the people can step into it with what they love and walk out of it. Each crossing takes an interval of your rest. You would wake later than you would have, by as long again.

**The Sleeper** 
Two. I give two long ones. A third long one, and I wake late and small.
She did not argue. It had named its price and its limit in the same breath, and both belonged to it.

**The Sleeper** 
When I wake, will they still sing?

**Illuminara** 
I think they'd like to. They'd sing from beside you, not from inside.

**The Sleeper** 
Beside.
It turned the word over, a stone in a mouth.

**The Sleeper** 
I have not had a beside.

**Illuminara** 
Then ask them. Not me. I can't promise you what they'll want.

**The Sleeper** 
Open the court. I will hear them. I could not hear them in the floor.

scenes.title: The Kitchen Interval
paragraphs: *The Metronome court - 21:10*
The Sleeper opened the court. Everyone in it could feel the warmth on the back of the neck, and the phrase came through the stones without anyone to carry it, three notes rising and the stop.

Hale knelt, which he had not done in front of anyone since his father's funeral. Ilse knelt beside him with her choir at her back. Illuminara stood between them and the floor and said, whenever she translated, how sure she was.

**Hale Ostrov** 
I came up here to close you for good.
The warmth did not move. Illuminara said so.

**Hale Ostrov** 
I would have been right to, if you had not answered. I want that said. I was not wrong to be afraid. Two hundred thousand people live in your thought and did not know it. I am sorry for what we did to you. I am not sorry we live.

**Illuminara** 
It says: both.

**Hale Ostrov** 
Both.
His shoulders came down, a very little, the way a rope comes down when someone at the other end lets go. Then he stood, and the engineer came back into his face.

**Hale Ostrov** 
I will not move a street on your word, or on its. I want one room first. Crossed by someone who chooses it, who can tell us what only she could know, and who can walk back out the same door. And I want failure named now, so nobody argues it afterwards.

**Illuminara** 
It says: a breath. It will lend a breath, not an interval.

**Hale Ostrov** 
Then this. If she cannot find the thing, or the thing is not where she left it, or the room does not smell like her room, the wedge goes back in my belt and we do this the hard way.
Nel Vasco was already pushing through the choir, the woman who had sung the Closing to her dying son. She lived on the Fishers' Stair, one room above a net-maker.

**Nel Vasco** 
There is a notch in my windowsill. He cut it with my kitchen knife when he was seven, and I never told him it was a shame to. If the notch is straight, that room isn't mine.

The Sleeper lent the breath. The room went still the way a held note goes still, and its door opened on a pane of glass-light. Nel walked in. For a moment there was only the court, and a hundred people not breathing.

**Nel Vasco** 
It's crooked. He cut it crooked.

Her voice broke on the word. She stood a moment longer, nose lifted, and said that the draught under the door was the one that always blew, and that it smelled of tar. Then she came back out the same door, into the court, with her hand over her mouth.

**Hale Ostrov** 
One woman, one room, one breath. I'll take it as the reason to ask the next person. Not as the answer.

**Nel Vasco** 
That's what I'd tell you to take it as.
Hale nodded, and for the first time that day he did not look at the wedge.

**Hale Ostrov** 
My mother's kitchen is in Low Cadence, on Tallow Row. She has lived in it for sixty-one years. It has a kettle that sings two notes at once. She will not leave it for a bell on a plain.
The warmth considered this for as long as it takes to walk across a court. Illuminara waited, and did not guess.

**The Sleeper** 
How long is a kitchen?

**Hale Ostrov** 
Ten minutes, if the kettle is on.

**The Sleeper** 
A third long one I cannot. A short one, the length of a kitchen, I can. Three streets: Tallow Row, the Fishers' Stair, the lamp-market. Not more.

**Hale Ostrov** 
And Salt Terrace?

**The Sleeper** 
I cannot. If I do, I wake late and small and I am no more than the thing you made me. I will not do it. I will not say I am sorry, because I will be, and it will not help.

**Ilse Marrow** 
Salt Terrace is sixty-four people. Mostly old. Mostly lamplighters. They've been there since before the Lull. Nobody has asked them.

A very old man came forward from the back of the choir with a lamp in each hand, small and bent, with the slow rolling walk of someone who has climbed the same steps for seventy years. A woman came behind him with her arms crossed and her chin up.

**Illuminara** 
Before anyone answers, I will say what I know. If you stay, you may die when it wakes. Or it may keep you in a way none of us has a word for, and it cannot tell me which. I would not ask you to choose on a better story than that.

**Teun Gaubert** 
I've lit the lamps on Salt Terrace since I was twenty-one. I'll light them till the light goes. It's a good light to go in. Better that than a bell on a plain.
Ilse said his name, once, and he did not look at her.

**Teun Gaubert** 
I heard the square, Ilse. I'm not being brave, I'm being tired, and I've the right. But I'm not the whole terrace. Ask them.

**Orla Pike** 
I'm not tired. I'll say that so nobody says it for me. My Aldo's lamp is on the third stoop. He lit it thirty-one years and I'll not leave it to burn out with nobody there to see. And I'll not be carried to a glass bell like a parcel. Ask the terrace one at a time, and mean it when you ask.

They asked, that night, one stoop at a time, with Ilse walking the terrace and Illuminara holding it. Bettin Hoyle, who had never in her life gone anywhere without a list, said she was frightened out of her wits and to write her down for staying all the same, and then asked whether she might hold somebody's sleeve while she waited. Sixty-one said they would stay, some of them steady and some of them shaking. Three said they would go, and a boy of twenty with a bag on his shoulder stood a long while on the top step before Teun said, without any heat, *Go on. Light somebody else's.* Nobody argued with him. Illuminara wrote the three names on her wrist.

**Illuminara** 
I will hold the terrace until you tell me to let go. Not a breath before.

**Teun Gaubert** 
That's all a man needs.
Hale got up slowly. He walked to the wedge of iron and picked it up in both hands and stood holding it, a man with a door in his arms.

**Illuminara** 
What will you do with it now?

**Hale Ostrov** 
Melt it. Draw it for the bell-field's tuning fork. A thing that was meant to stop a song ought to help keep one in tune.
He looked at Illuminara, and at the floor behind her, and said to both, in the voice of a man who has only just discovered he has one:

**Hale Ostrov** 
Two long intervals, and a kitchen. Tell it we'll be ready by midnight. Tell it we'll ask, every time, before we take.

**The Sleeper** 
Your mother's kettle. Bring it.
Illuminara repeated that word for word, and did not mention that the warmth, saying it, had felt very much like a smile.

scenes.title: The Waking
paragraphs: *The plain and Salt Terrace - From midnight to dawn*

They took the first interval at midnight, and it lasted the length of a long walk. The whole of the Sleeper's attention lay on the Stair of Bells like sunlight on a field, and a district at a time stepped through its own front doors into rooms that were the same rooms, set in glass, on the plain. The market clock rang sharp when it arrived and never rang true again. People loved it afterwards for the sound.

Between intervals the city thinned, and Illuminara held it: the Stair, then the market, then the long bridge of the choirs' hall. The one rule she kept was the one she had given. Nothing fell until the last person who wanted to leave had left.

The nine thousand who could reach the edge walked out into the cold hills with their children and their blankets, and the hills had been ready for them since the first rest. Dorrit Vane, a shepherd with a voice like a gate, had banked fires on the ridge, opened the byre doors, filled the troughs and put her own grandsons to carrying blankets down the slope. She told Illuminara, flatly, that she would take whoever came and Illuminara could hold her gap or not, it made no difference to the sheep. So Illuminara held it, each rest, until three lamps showed on the ridge in a row, which meant the last of that crossing was in hand, and not a breath before.

The second interval took the south wards and the choirs' hall. The third was a kitchen long. Marit Ostrov came through it last of her street, a small, upright woman with a kettle clutched in both hands like an infant, and when Hale reached for her arm she looked at him down a nose that had been looking at him down that nose for fifty years. *It's coming, Ma,* he said, and she let him carry the other handle.

She set it on a flat glass bell. The kettle had been brought out of one dream into another with its water still warm. When she lit the little flame beneath it, it sang its two notes at once, and the bell beneath it sang a third.

The third interval closed. The Sleeper's attention lifted from the city like a hand from a sleeping child's hair, and what was left of Aubade, the Lower Arcade's empty plot, the outer terraces, and Salt Terrace itself, hung in the thinning dark, held up by almost nothing. Ilse came off the plain with a slate in her hand, and she read it out where Illuminara could hear it, because she had said she would not let the count go unspoken.

**Ilse Marrow** 
Two hundred thousand. One hundred and ninety thousand, five hundred through the glass. Nine thousand, four hundred and thirty-six out along the edge, into the hills; Dorrit Vane counted them in and the byres held. Three from Salt Terrace, with a bag. And sixty-one on the terrace. They did not come through the glass doors, Illuminara. They are not coming.

**Illuminara** 
No.

She went to the terrace. They were sitting on their stoops with their lamps lit, sixty-one of them, in blankets. Teun was at the end, with a lamp in each hand, and Orla Pike was on the third stoop with her husband's lamp beside her own. Bettin Hoyle had somebody's sleeve. Some of them were afraid and had stopped pretending otherwise, and sat anyway. They were looking at the light the way you look at a fire you have kept in all night, to see how it will go out.

The plain began to move. It had never been a plain. It was the lap of a thing, and the horizon moved because the thing was moving. The brow, a ridge half a mile across, lifted, and under it two enormous slow lids parted on a darkness that had stars in it. The Sleeper woke the way a tide comes in: not at once, but all at once in the end. The sound of its breath went over the bell-field and every glass bell trembled on its stem.
Then it sang the fourth note.

Bright and rising, and entirely its own, it went out across the plain and down the terraces, and three hundred bells answered it, and on Salt Terrace sixty-one lamps rang with it as glass rings. Teun Gaubert raised both his lamps. He looked at Illuminara. She waited. It came as a nod, slow and courteous, the nod of a man handing back a key. On the third stoop Orla Pike did not nod. She lifted her husband's lamp and held it up where the Sleeper's eye could see it.
She let go.

Salt Terrace folded into the song the way lamplight folds into morning. The stoops, the lamps, the sixty-one people on them, afraid and unafraid alike, holding up their light. There was no fall and no noise. One moment the terrace was there, and one moment it was a phrase in the air, an extra bar in the second line of three notes and a fourth, going up.

Whether what the Sleeper carried afterwards in that phrase was the people of Salt Terrace, or the shape of them, or only the memory of the shape, no one can say. Ilse says she hears Teun's cough in the second bar. Hale says she is wrong, and then says nothing for a while. The Sleeper has said that it keeps them. It has not said more, and nobody has had the heart to ask it to.

Illuminara stood a long time with her palms still in front of her, holding up nothing. The Sleeper's eye turned, the size of a lake, and looked with great care at the small figure on the edge of the bell-field. A voice came through the glass, warm and slow and quite clear in the morning.

**The Sleeper** 
What is a beside?

**Illuminara** 
This.

On the plain below, Ilse Marrow raised her hand, and her fifty singers, and the city that was left, stood up in the new light and sang three notes, each higher than the last. They stopped. They left the place for the fourth.
The Sleeper filled it. It was not finished. It never would be. That was the point of it.
Beside her, Hale Ostrov, who had come up the Stair to close a door, stood with one hand on his mother's shoulder and a kettle singing two notes behind him, and listened to a neighbour wake.

critic_line: A city that had survived by keeping its maker asleep learned to ask before it crossed: Nel Vasco proved one room by her son's crooked notch and its tar draught, Dorrit Vane received the people of the edge, and the sixty-one who stayed were told the unknowable truth and allowed to be afraid, while Illuminara held stone and silence without choosing for any of them.

translation_sl.title: MESTO, ZGRAJENO V SPEČI PESMI
translation_sl.deck: Mesto Aubade je zgrajeno iz počasne glasbe spečega bitja, ki se je začelo prebujati. Njegovi inženirji nameravajo ob sedmem zvonu prekiniti ritem; njegovi zbori so opazili, da se vsak premor konča s tonom, ki ga zapoje nekdo drug. Illuminara ima en dolg večer, da ugotovi, kaj Speči sprašuje in čemu se je mesto pripravljeno odreči, da bi ga slišalo.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v enem popoldnevu in noči: rez, pripravljen za sedmi zvon; stavek brez četrtega tona; trg, ki glasuje, in kopija, ki zazveni prenizko ter mesto stane ulice; vprašanje, zastavljeno tako, da prostor zanj ostane odprt; kuhinjski pogovor, v katerem ena soba po zaupanju prestopi pred katerokoli ulico; in prebujenje, v katerem nekateri odidejo, drugi ostanejo, število pa je izrečeno na glas.

scenes.title: Tretji premor
paragraphs: *Aubade, Stopnišče zvonov · Tretji premor dneva, 14:10*

Tlak Stopnišča je pod Illuminarinimi škornji brnel z nizkim, enakomernim tonom, ki ga je čutila v koreninah zob; vsakih nekaj stopnic se je brnenje stanjšalo in se vrnilo, kakor se stanjša dih v trenutku, preden se nekdo odloči, da ga bo izpustil.
Pred eno uro je vstopila skozi rob mesta, priklicana z dvainštiridesetimi zapetimi toni, katerih preprosti pomen je razumela kot iztegnjeno roko: *prosim, kdorkoli, ki lahko stvari drži pokonci.*

Zdaj se je stopniščni krak nad njo povesil, bledi uglašeni kamen je na sredini mehčal kakor sveča v topli sobi, ženska s tržno košaro pa se je ustavila na stopnici z odprtimi usti in ni zakričala, kar je Illuminara opazila in spoštovala. Dlani je plosko nastavila proti zraku pred stopniščem. Teža ji je legla na roke kakor moker šotor. Izdihnila je in kamen se je znova postavil v svoj ton.

Na vrhu je na tlakovanem dvorišču stal bronast vilasti steber, višji od vsake cerkve: Metronom. Pod njegovo korenino je moški z manšetami, črnimi kakor črnilo, klečal nad zagozdo hladnega železa, veliko kakor vrata, in ni pogledal gor, dokler ni stala nad njim.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Vi ste tista, za katero je Marrow zapela. Rekel sem ji, naj ne.

**Illuminara**  
Rekla je, da me boste vseeno spustili noter.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Spustim vsakogar, ki lahko nosi težo. Videl sem vas nekaj teže nositi. Lahko nosite vso?

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Ne vse in ne dolgo. Čemu je namenjena zagozda?

**Hale Ostrov**  
Premori postajajo daljši. Zjutraj dvajset minut, zdaj petdeset. Blizu sedmega zvona bo eden dovolj dolg, da bo Metronom razgaljen do korenine; zabil bom tole noter in zaklenil ritem. Premori se bodo nehali. Mesto bo še naprej mesto.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa tisti, čigar ritem je?

**Hale Ostrov**  
Spi.
To je izrekel, ne da bi trznil.

**Illuminara**  
Bi lahko ljudje med premorom odšli? Skozi rob, po poti, po kateri sem prišla jaz?

**Hale Ostrov**  
Tisti, ki živijo blizu, lahko. Devet tisoč, morda deset. Drugi živijo pregloboko; rob se znova zapre, preden ga dosežejo. Dvesto tisoč ljudi, Illuminara. Povejte mi, kje bodo stali, če mi ni dovoljeno rezati. Povejte mi, kje jih etika ohrani.
Ni odgovorila, ker odgovora še ni imela, on pa si je zaslužil resnično tišino, ne hitrega odgovora. Pod njunimi stopali se je tlak stanjšal in vrnil.
Ilse Marrow je prišla po Stopnišču s svojim zborom za seboj, široka ženska z ruto iz volne desetih barv.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Hale. Še je niste zabili.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Ob sedmem zvonu, Ilse. To veste.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Vem, da to izgovarjate kakor človek, ki bere svoje ime s kamna.
Obrnila se je k Illuminari in ni tratila niti diha za pozdrav.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Uglašujem zbore Nizke kadence. Jaz sem zapela. Ob koncu vsakega premora umirimo mesto in devetkrat smo ga že umirili, devetkrat je obstalo. Preden kdo kam zabije železo, želim, da prisluhnete temu, kar umirjamo.

**Illuminara**  
Ničesar ne bi raje storila.
Nad dvoriščem je brnenje padlo za pol tona, kakor se je po Ilsinih besedah zgodilo, ko se je premor bližal koncu. Illuminara se je obrnila in prisluhnila.

scenes.title: Stavek brez četrtega tona
paragraphs: *Ob vznožju Stopnišča, med zborom · 14:52*

Pričakovala je glas, stavek, nekaj, kar bi lahko postavila nasproti temu, kar je hotel Hale. Najprej je prišla toplota: pritisk na zatilju, kakor bi tam počivala roka, da bi videla, ali bo trznila. Nato stavek.

Trije toni, vsak višji od prejšnjega, vsak zadržan malo dlje, kakor otrok drži ograjo na vrhu stopnišča, za katero ni prepričan, ali se želi povzpeti po njem. Po tretjem je sledila zaustavitev. Ni bila tišina. Tišina je odsotnost tona. To pa je imelo obliko tona, iz katerega je bil ton odstranjen, kakor vdolbina v blazini, kjer je ležala glava.

Petkrat je poslušala, ne da bi se premaknila. Šestič je opazila, kar je ves čas slišala, ne da bi zares slišala: zaustavitev ni bila tam, kjer je pevcu zmanjkalo sape. Bila je tam, kjer je pevec čakal.

**Illuminara**  
Ni nedokončano. Sprašuje.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Kaj sprašuje?

**Illuminara**  
Še ne vem. Toda vsakokrat pusti prostor za odgovor, vedno povsem enake velikosti.
Ilse je strmela vanjo. Nato je čez njen široki obraz šlo nekaj, kar še ni bilo razumevanje, le senca, ki jo razumevanje vrže predse.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Oh. Oh, to je Zaključek. To je ton, ki mu ga damo.

Zaključek je bil en dolg padajoči ton, ki se ga je vsak otrok v Aubadeju naučil, preden se je naučil brati; peli so ga ob policijski uri in na koncu vsakega premora, kakor druga mesta zazvonijo z zvonom. Zbor se je na širokih stopnicah razvrstil v vrste, Ilse pa je dvignila roko.

Bilo je najlepše, kar je Illuminara slišala v mestu: petdeset glasov, ki so se spuščali po stopnišču enega samega tona, tako nežno, da se je zdelo, kakor bi kamen pod njimi legel. In začutila je, kaj je ob prihodu storil Speči. Topla roka na njenem zatilju se je zaprla. Ni se zaprla kakor pest. Zaprla se je kakor roka zelo utrujenega človeka, ki so mu prijazno rekli, da se sme ustaviti. Brnenje se je ustalilo. Stopnišče je otrdelo v svojo običajno, gladko in hladno podobo. Premora je bilo konec.
Svoj stavek je končal v glasu nekoga drugega in se vrnil pod njega.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Nekaj ste slišali.

**Illuminara**  
Slišala sem samo enkrat, zato se lahko motim. Povedala vam bom, kaj sem slišala, vi pa mi povejte, kje je napačno. Stavek ima tri tone in vrzel. Vrzel je vsakokrat enaka. Vi jo zapolnite s padajočim tonom. Ko to storite, se spusti.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Tristo let ga pojemo vsako noč, ker je bila to pesem. Pravite mi, da smo ga uspavali.

**Illuminara**  
Pravim vam, da mu tristo let pojete, ker ga imate radi, in da pesem obenem zapira vrata. Mislim, da je res oboje. Ne mislim, da eno izniči drugo.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Če je ne zapojemo, se premori podaljšajo. In mesto razpade.

**Illuminara**  
Deli bi morda res razpadli. Nekaj jih lahko držim, medtem ko ljudje odhajajo. Ne vseh in ne dolgo. Toda druga možnost je za vedno zapreti vrata in nikoli izvedeti, na kaj je čakal.

**Ilse Marrow**  
O tem ne bom sama odločala za dvesto tisoč ljudi. In ne bom storila za Halovim hrbtom. Ob šestem zvonu bom pred njegovim obrazom vprašanje postavila trgu. Če trg reče, naj pojemo, bom pela, vi pa boste molčali.

**Illuminara**  
Bom.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Dobro. Manj bi si mislila o vas, če bi rekli karkoli drugega.

scenes.title: Trg in kopija, ki je zazvenela prenizko
paragraphs: *Dvorišče Metronoma · Šesti zvon, 18:00, in pozneje*
Trg je napolnil dvorišče in stopnice pod njim, deset tisoč svetilk so držali v višini ramen, razprava pa je tekla tako, kakor tečejo razprave, ko je stvar, o kateri se prepirajo, pod nogami vseh.

**Anselm Duret**  
Pet premorov, Ilse. Šest. Moji modeli pravijo, da bodo spodnje arkade prve, in v Spodnji arkadi imam jaz trgovino, moja sestra pa svojo. Želite z glasovanjem mojo ulico izbrisati z zemljevida, da bi gora imela drugačen čas za spanje?

**Ilse Marrow**  
Želim glasovati, da slišimo, kaj gora pravi. Želim ji pustiti prostor in videti, ali odgovori. To je vse, kar vas prosim, da storite.

Ženska pri zadnjem delu, Nel Vasco, je rekla, da je Zaključek zapela svojemu umirajočemu sinu in da ne bo poslušala, kako ga imenujejo kletka. Nato je tiše rekla, da bi rada vedela. Hale Ostrov je vse poslušal in ni rekel ničesar. Illuminara je stala s sklenjenimi rokami in zadržanim jezikom, kar je bilo težje od stopnišča; ko so se svetilke dvignile, ni pogledala, koliko jih je.

Dvigovale so se uro in četrt, nato pa ostale dvignjene. Večina ni bila velika. Moški blizu ospredja je dvignil svetilko, nato jo z vidnim sramom spustil, njegova žena pa ga je prijela za zapestje in jo znova dvignila.
Zdaj, ko je bil Metronom razgaljen do korenine in se je kamen že začel tanjšati, je Hale spregovoril, ne da bi se obrnil.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Železa ne bom zabil, dokler vam ne pokažem, zakaj druga pot ne deluje. Moj ceh je na ravnici onkraj Spečega čela zgradil polje steklenih zvonov, tristo jih je, uglašenih na mestne tonalitete. Vanj bom prekopiral najnižji krak Stopnišča. Če bo delovalo, bom čakal. Če bo spodletelo, se boste umaknili.

**Illuminara**  
Ste ga vprašali? Tistega, čigar stopnice so?

**Hale Ostrov**  
Naj vprašam tla, ali smem vzeti kos tal? V katerem jeziku? Šest premorov imam, preden bodo po mojih modelih spodnje arkade odpovedale. Stopniščni krak je poceni. Najprej jemljem majhno stvar.

**Illuminara**  
Ne vem. Preden vzamete, bi rada poskusila vprašati.

Pomislila je, da bi rekla ne. Imela je moč, da ga ustavi, in začutila je težo te moči, nato jo je odložila, kakor vrneš kovanec, ki ga ne nameravaš porabiti. Stopniščni krak ni bil življenje. Če bi bil, bi ga ustavila, in vedela je, kako tanka je meja. Mesto je bilo njegovo, Ilsino in Spečega. Ni bilo njeno, da odloči.

Premor je nastopil. Brnenje se je spustilo in tla dvorišča so se iz kamna spremenila v nekaj toplega, mehkega in temnega. Hale je udaril po glavnem zvoncu. Daleč spodaj na ravnici je en stekleni zvon zazvenel prenizko, za četrt tona pod mestom, kjer bi moral: zvok nečesa, kar je bilo vzeto, ne da bi bilo ponujeno.

Nato je Speči trznil. Ni bil rjovenje. Rjovenje bi bilo odgovor. Bil je krč, vsa topla tema dvorišča se je zaprla kakor pest in vsak kamen v Aubadeju se je enkrat stresel. Spodaj v Spodnji arkadi, ulici vrvarjev in svečarjev z devetdesetimi sobami nad njimi, so tla izginila izpod pritličja.

Illuminara ni toliko stekla kakor prispela. Z dlanmi je prestregla zrak pred padajočim pročeljem arkade in teža devetdesetih sob ji je legla na roke kot upočasnjen plaz. Začutila je, kako so jo sprejela kolena.

**Illuminara**  
Hodite. Ne tecite. Uporabite stopnišče na levi.

Tristo ljudi je hodilo, s plašči, mačkami in zvitimi žimnicami, starka je v ruti nosila kanarčka, dva fanta pa tretjega. Predzadnji je odšel moški z medeninasto tehtnico v rokah. Stala je, dokler ni odšel zadnji, in jih štela. Nato je spustila in devetdeset sob je prenehalo biti sob.

**Anselm Duret**  
Glasoval sem, da nadaljujemo petje. Moja ulica je izginila.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Izginila je, ker smo vzeli, Anselm. Ne zato, ker smo vprašali.

**Anselm Duret**  
Je zaradi tega streha kaj boljša?

**Illuminara**  
Ne.

Ko se je vrnila po Stopnišču, je Hale stal na dvorišču z železom pri nogah. Ni bil videti kakor človek, ki so mu dokazali, da ima prav. Bil je videti kakor človek, ki so mu prav dokazali za določeno ceno.

**Illuminara**  
Dajte mi ta premor. Zbor ne bo pel. Trajal bo dolgo in se za menoj ne bo zaprl. Dajte mi čas do njegovega konca.
Pogledal je železo, golo korenino vilice in razpoko v mestu spodaj. Ko je odgovoril, je odgovoril kamnu, ne njej.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Do konca. Zagozda ostane v moji roki.

scenes.title: Vprašanje
paragraphs: *Znotraj premora, pod Metronomom · 19:40*

Da bi prišla do Spečega, je storila najpreprostejše: nehala je biti kjerkoli drugje. Pokleknila je ob korenini velike vilice in položila dlan na dvorišče, ki ni bilo več tla. Bilo je toplo, nekoliko se je vdalo in dišalo po bakru ter dežju na skrilavcu. Nekje v njem je tekel utrip, počasnejši od vsakega srca, ki ga je poznala: en udarec v času, potrebnem, da prehodiš dvorišče.
Zabrundala je tri tone, vsakega višjega od prejšnjega, vsakega zadržanega malo dlje. Nato se je ustavila in držala zaustavitev.

Četrtega ni zapela. Vse v njej si je to želelo; najbolj naravna stvar na svetu je zapolniti prostor, ki je bil puščen zate. Željo je čutila, kako se ji dviga v grlu kakor smeh v cerkvi, in pustila jo je stati tam, ne da bi jo uporabila. *Ne bom ga dokončala namesto tebe.* To si je ponavljala v sebi, kakor človek izgovarja ime spečemu, da bi ga počasi prebudil.
Tišina se je nadaljevala. Nad njo je Metronom enkrat zelo tiho zazvonil, kakor zazveni kozarec, ko gre prst mimo njega. Začela so jo boleti kolena. Daleč proč je nekdo otroku govoril, naj bo tiho.
In Speči je zapel četrti ton.

Ni bil Zaključek. Zaključek je padal. Ta se je dvigal: ton, višji od tretjega, svetel, rahlo napačen in povsem njegov; ko je zazvenel, je z njim hkrati zazvonil vsak zvon v mestu, tristo steklenih zvonov na ravnici, železo v Halovi roki in sama stopnišča, ves Aubade je zazvenel kakor udarjen kozarec. Illuminara, pripravljena na vse razen tega, se je zasmejala na glas. Bil je kratek, nemočen, navdušen zvok, smeh nekoga, ki je prvič slišal, kako je nekaj dokončalo svoj stavek.

Kar jo je doseglo zatem, ni bil govor. Bila je razporeditev toplote in pritiska, ki jo je spreminjala v besede, kakor vreme spremeniš v odločitev o plašču. Vsakič je na glas povedala, da ugiba, in vsakokrat se je toplota nagnila bliže, da bi jo popravila.

**Speči**  
Nekdo je nehal spraševati.

**Illuminara**  
Da. Pred tristo leti. Potem so mislili, da si vreme.

**Speči**  
Pel sem. Nato je bilo dokončano. Nato sem postal tla.

**Illuminara**  
Vem. Žal mi je, da je trajalo tako dolgo, preden ti je nekdo pustil prostor.

**Speči**  
Topli so. Med premori jih slišim. Ne želim, da bi jih zeblo. Hočem svoje misli nazaj.

**Illuminara**  
Ko se zbudiš, ne morejo vsi ostati v njih. Del mesta je tvoja misel.

**Speči**  
Vem, kaj sem jaz in kaj so oni. Čutim rob. Posodim lahko premor. Posojen premor je premor, v katerem se ne zbudim.
Tedaj je razumela, kaj ji ponuja in koliko bo to stalo tistega, ki ponuja. Vprašala ga je edino tako, kakor se je domislila: naravnost in brez pritiska.

**Illuminara**  
Ob tebi je polje steklenih zvonov. Če posodiš svojo pozornost, eno mestno četrt naenkrat, lahko ljudje s tem, kar imajo radi, stopijo vanj in izstopijo. Vsak prehod vzame en interval tvojega premora. Zbudil bi se pozneje, še enkrat toliko časa.

**Speči**  
Dva. Dam dva dolga. Tretji dolgi in zbudim se pozen in majhen.
Ni ugovarjala. V istem dihu je imenoval svojo ceno in svojo mejo; oboje je pripadalo njemu.

**Speči**  
Ko se zbudim, bodo še peli?

**Illuminara**  
Mislim, da bi radi. Peli bi poleg tebe, ne v tebi.

**Speči**  
Poleg.
Besedo je obračal, kakor kamen v ustih.

**Speči**  
Nikoli nisem imel poleg.

**Illuminara**  
Potem vprašaj njih. Ne mene. Ne morem ti obljubiti, kaj bodo želeli.

**Speči**  
Odpri dvorišče. Slišal jih bom. V tleh jih nisem mogel slišati.

scenes.title: Kuhinjski interval
paragraphs: *Dvorišče Metronoma · 21:10*
Speči je odprl dvorišče. Vsi na njem so začutili toploto na zatilju, stavek pa je brez kogarkoli, ki bi ga nosil, prišel skozi kamne: trije dvigajoči se toni in zaustavitev.

Hale je pokleknil, česar pred nikomer ni storil od očetovega pogreba. Ilse je pokleknila poleg njega, z zborom za svojim hrbtom. Illuminara je stala med njima in tlemi in ob vsakem prevodu povedala, kako prepričana je.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Prišel sem sem gor, da bi te za vedno zaprl.
Toplota se ni premaknila. Illuminara je to povedala.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Prav bi imel, če ne bi odgovoril. Želim, da je to izrečeno. Ni bilo narobe, da me je bilo strah. Dvesto tisoč ljudi živi v tvoji misli in tega ni vedelo. Žal mi je za to, kar smo ti storili. Ni mi žal, da živimo.

**Illuminara**  
Pravi: oboje.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Oboje.
Njegova ramena so se malo spustila, kakor se vrv spusti, ko jo nekdo na drugem koncu izpusti. Nato je vstal in inženir se je vrnil v njegov obraz.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Ne bom premaknil ulice na vašo besedo ali njegovo. Najprej hočem eno sobo. Prečka naj jo nekdo, ki to sam izbere, ki nam lahko pove nekaj, kar lahko ve samo on, in ki se lahko vrne skozi ista vrata. In hočem, da neuspeh imenujemo zdaj, da se pozneje nihče ne bo prepiral o njem.

**Illuminara**  
Pravi: dih. Posodil bo dih, ne intervala.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Potem takole. Če ne najde stvari, če stvar ni tam, kjer jo je pustila, ali če soba ne diši kakor njena, gre zagozda nazaj za moj pas in to storimo po težji poti.
Nel Vasco, ženska, ki je svojemu umirajočemu sinu zapela Zaključek, se je že prebijala skozi zbor. Živela je na Ribiškem stopnišču, eno sobo nad izdelovalcem mrež.

**Nel Vasco**  
Na moji okenski polici je zareza. Ko mu je bilo sedem let, jo je z mojim kuhinjskim nožem naredil moj sin, jaz pa mu nikoli nisem rekla, da bi ga moralo biti sram. Če je zareza ravna, tista soba ni moja.

Speči je posodil dih. Soba je obmirovala, kakor obmiruje zadržan ton, njena vrata pa so se odprla v stekleno svetlobo. Nel je vstopila. Za trenutek sta obstajala le dvorišče in sto ljudi, ki niso dihali.

**Nel Vasco**  
Kriva je. Krivo jo je zarezal.

Glas se ji je zlomil ob besedi. Še trenutek je stala z dvignjenim nosom in rekla, da je prepih pod vrati isti, ki je vedno pihal, in da diši po katranu. Nato se je skozi ista vrata vrnila na dvorišče z roko čez usta.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Ena ženska, ena soba, en dih. Vzel bom kot razlog, da vprašam naslednjega človeka. Ne kot odgovor.

**Nel Vasco**  
Tudi jaz bi vam rekla, da vzemite tako.
Hale je prikimal in prvič tistega dne ni pogledal zagozde.

**Hale Ostrov**  
Kuhinja moje matere je v Nizki kadenci, v Lojni ulici. V njej živi enainšestdeset let. Ima čajnik, ki poje dva tona hkrati. Ne bo je zapustila zaradi zvona na ravnici.
Toplota je o tem premišljevala toliko časa, kolikor potrebuješ, da prehodiš dvorišče. Illuminara je čakala in ni ugibala.

**Speči**  
Kako dolga je kuhinja?

**Hale Ostrov**  
Deset minut, če je čajnik na ognju.

**Speči**  
Tretjega dolgega ne morem. Kratkega, dolžine kuhinje, lahko. Tri ulice: Lojna ulica, Ribiško stopnišče, trg svetilk. Ne več.

**Hale Ostrov**  
In Solna terasa?

**Speči**  
Ne morem. Če storim, se zbudim pozen in majhen in sem samo še tisto, kar ste naredili iz mene. Ne bom. Ne bom rekel, da mi je žal, ker mi bo in to ne bo pomagalo.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Na Solni terasi je štiriinšestdeset ljudi. Večinoma starejših. Večinoma prižigalcev svetilk. Tam so še iz časa pred Uspavanjem. Nihče jih ni vprašal.

Z zadnjega dela zbora je stopil zelo star moški s svetilko v vsaki roki, majhen in upognjen, s počasno zibajočo hojo človeka, ki se je sedemdeset let vzpenjal po istih stopnicah. Za njim je prišla ženska s prekrižanimi rokami in dvignjeno brado.

**Illuminara**  
Preden kdo odgovori, bom povedala, kar vem. Če ostanete, boste morda umrli, ko se zbudi. Ali pa vas bo ohranil na način, za katerega nihče od nas nima besede, in ne more mi povedati, kaj od tega se bo zgodilo. Ne bi vas prosila, da izbirate na podlagi lepše zgodbe od te.

**Teun Gaubert**  
Svetilke na Solni terasi prižigam od enaindvajsetega leta. Prižigal jih bom, dokler bo svetloba. Lepo je oditi v taki svetlobi. Bolje kakor v zvonu na ravnici.
Ilse je enkrat izgovorila njegovo ime, on pa je ni pogledal.

**Teun Gaubert**  
Slišal sem trg, Ilse. Nisem pogumen, utrujen sem in imam pravico. Toda nisem vsa terasa. Vprašajte jih.

**Orla Pike**  
Jaz nisem utrujena. To bom povedala, da tega nihče ne bo rekel namesto mene. Svetilka mojega Alda je na tretjem pragu. Prižigal jo je enaintrideset let in ne bom je pustila dogoreti, ne da bi bil kdo tam in to videl. In ne bom dovolila, da me kakor zavoj odnesejo v stekleni zvon. Vprašajte teraso, enega po enega, in ko vprašate, to mislite resno.

Tisto noč so vprašali pri vsakem pragu posebej, Ilse je hodila po terasi, Illuminara pa jo je držala. Bettin Hoyle, ki v življenju nikamor ni šla brez seznama, je rekla, da je od strahu brez sebe, vendar naj jo vseeno zapišejo med tiste, ki ostanejo; nato je vprašala, ali lahko med čakanjem drži nekoga za rokav. Enainšestdeset jih je reklo, da bodo ostali, nekateri mirni, drugi tresoči. Trije so rekli, da bodo odšli; dvajsetletni fant z vrečo na ramenu je dolgo stal na vrhnji stopnici, preden je Teun brez trohice jeze rekel: *Kar pojdi. Prižgi komu drugemu.* Nihče mu ni ugovarjal. Illuminara si je tri imena zapisala na zapestje.

**Illuminara**  
Teraso bom držala, dokler mi ne rečete, naj jo izpustim. Niti dih prej.

**Teun Gaubert**  
To je vse, kar človek potrebuje.
Hale je počasi vstal. Stopil je do železne zagozde, jo z obema rokama dvignil in stal z njo kakor človek z vrati v naročju.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj boste zdaj storili z njo?

**Hale Ostrov**  
Stalil jo bom. Iz nje bom skoval uglaševalne vilice za polje zvonov. Stvar, ki naj bi ustavila pesem, bi morala pomagati, da ostane uglašena.
Pogledal je Illuminari in tlem za njo ter obema spregovoril z glasom človeka, ki je šele pravkar odkril, da ga ima:

**Hale Ostrov**  
Dva dolga intervala in kuhinja. Povejte mu, da bomo do polnoči pripravljeni. Povejte mu, da bomo vsakič vprašali, preden vzamemo.

**Speči**  
Čajnik njegove matere. Prinesite ga.
Illuminara je to ponovila besedo za besedo in ni omenila, da je bila toplota ob tem zelo podobna nasmehu.

scenes.title: Prebujenje
paragraphs: *Ravnica in Solna terasa · Od polnoči do zore*

Prvi interval so vzeli ob polnoči in trajal je toliko kakor dolg sprehod. Vsa pozornost Spečega je ležala na Stopnišču zvonov kakor sončna svetloba na polju in ena mestna četrt za drugo je skozi lastna vhodna vrata stopila v sobe, ki so bile iste sobe, postavljene iz stekla na ravnici. Tržna ura je ob prihodu zazvonila ostro in nikoli več ni zazvonila pravilno. Pozneje so jo ljudje zaradi tega zvoka vzljubili.

Med intervali se je mesto tanjšalo, Illuminara pa ga je držala: Stopnišče, nato tržnico, nato dolgi most zborovske dvorane. Držala se je enega pravila, ki ga je dala. Nič ni padlo, dokler ni odšel zadnji človek, ki je želel oditi.

Devet tisoč ljudi, ki so lahko dosegli rob, je s svojimi otroki in odejami odšlo v mrzle hribe; hribi pa so bili nanje pripravljeni od prvega premora. Dorrit Vane, pastirica z glasom kakor vrata, je na grebenu pripravila ognje, odprla vrata hlevov, napolnila korita in svojim vnukom naročila, naj nosijo odeje po pobočju. Illuminari je brez ovinkarjenja rekla, da bo sprejela vsakogar, ki pride, in da lahko Illuminara vrzel drži ali ne, ovcam je vseeno. Zato jo je Illuminara med vsakim premorom držala, dokler se na grebenu niso v vrsti pokazale tri svetilke, kar je pomenilo, da je zadnji iz tistega prehoda na varnem, in niti dih prej.

Drugi interval je odnesel južne četrti in zborovsko dvorano. Tretji je trajal eno kuhinjo. Marit Ostrov je iz njega prišla zadnja v svoji ulici, majhna, vzravnana ženska, ki je v obeh rokah stiskala čajnik kakor dojenčka. Ko je Hale segel po njeni roki, ga je pogledala čez nos, ki ga je tako gledal petdeset let. *Prihaja, mama,* je rekel, ona pa mu je dovolila nositi drugi ročaj.

Postavila ga je na raven stekleni zvon. Čajnik je bil iz enih sanj prinesen v druge, voda v njem pa je bila še topla. Ko je prižgala majhen plamen pod njim, je zapel dva tona hkrati, zvon pod njim pa tretjega.

Tretji interval se je zaprl. Pozornost Spečega se je dvignila z mesta kakor roka z las spečega otroka; od Aubadeja pa so parcela prazne Spodnje arkade, zunanje terase in sama Solna terasa ostale viseti v tanjšajoči se temi, podprte skoraj z ničimer. Ilse je z ravnice prišla s tablico v roki in jo prebrala tam, kjer jo je Illuminara lahko slišala, ker je rekla, da ne bo dovolila, da število ostane neizrečeno.

**Ilse Marrow**  
Dvesto tisoč. Sto devetdeset tisoč petsto skozi steklo. Devet tisoč štiristo šestintrideset čez rob v hribe; Dorrit Vane jih je preštela ob prihodu in hlevi so zdržali. Trije s Solne terase, z vrečo. In enainšestdeset na terasi. Niso prišli skozi steklena vrata, Illuminara. Ne bodo prišli.

**Illuminara**  
Ne.

Šla je na teraso. Sedeli so na svojih pragih s prižganimi svetilkami, vseh enainšestdeset, ovitih v odeje. Teun je bil na koncu s svetilko v vsaki roki, Orla Pike pa je sedela na tretjem pragu s svetilko svojega moža ob svoji. Bettin Hoyle je nekoga držala za rokav. Nekaterih je bilo strah in so se nehali pretvarjati drugače, a so vseeno sedeli. Gledali so svetlobo tako, kakor gledaš ogenj, ki si ga ohranjal vso noč, da bi videl, kako bo ugasnil.

Ravnica se je začela premikati. Nikoli ni bila ravnica. Bila je naročje bitja in obzorje se je premikalo, ker se je bitje premikalo. Čelo, pol milje širok greben, se je dvignilo in pod njim sta se na temi, v kateri so bile zvezde, odprli dve ogromni počasni veki. Speči se je zbudil tako, kakor pride plima: ne naenkrat, toda na koncu vsa hkrati. Zvok njegovega dihanja je šel čez polje zvonov in vsak stekleni zvon je zatrepetal na svojem steblu.
Nato je zapel četrti ton.

Svetel, dvigajoč se in povsem njegov je šel čez ravnico in po terasah navzdol, tristo zvonov mu je odgovorilo, na Solni terasi pa je z njim zazvonilo enainšestdeset svetilk, kakor zvoni steklo. Teun Gaubert je dvignil obe svetilki. Pogledal je Illuminari. Čakala je. Prišlo je kot prikimavanje, počasno in vljudno, prikimavanje človeka, ki vrača ključ. Na tretjem pragu Orla Pike ni prikimala. Dvignila je moževo svetilko in jo držala tam, kjer jo je Spečevo oko lahko videlo.
Izpustila je.

Solna terasa se je zgubala v pesem tako, kakor se svetloba svetilk zguba v jutro. Pragovi, svetilke, enainšestdeset ljudi na njih, prestrašeni in neprestrašeni, vsi so držali svojo svetlobo. Ni bilo padca in ne hrupa. En trenutek je bila terasa tam, naslednji pa je bila stavek v zraku, dodatni takt v drugi vrstici treh tonov in četrtega, ki se je dvigal.

Nihče ne more reči, ali je Speči pozneje v tem stavku nosil ljudi s Solne terase, njihovo obliko ali zgolj spomin na obliko. Ilse pravi, da v drugem taktu sliši Teunov kašelj. Hale pravi, da se moti, nato pa nekaj časa molči. Speči je rekel, da jih ohranja. Ni povedal več in nihče ni imel srca, da bi ga vprašal.

Illuminara je dolgo stala z dlanmi še vedno pred seboj in ni držala ničesar. Spečevo oko, veliko kakor jezero, se je obrnilo in z veliko skrbjo pogledalo majhno postavo na robu polja zvonov. Skozi steklo je prišel glas, topel, počasen in v jutru povsem jasen.

**Speči**  
Kaj pomeni poleg?

**Illuminara**  
Tole.

Na ravnici spodaj je Ilse Marrow dvignila roko in njenih petdeset pevcev ter mesto, ki je ostalo, so vstali v novi svetlobi in zapeli tri tone, vsakega višjega od prejšnjega. Ustavili so se. Pustili so prostor za četrtega.
Speči ga je zapolnil. Ni bilo dokončano. Nikoli ne bo. Prav v tem je bil smisel.
Poleg nje je Hale Ostrov, ki je prišel po Stopnišču zapret vrata, stal z eno roko na materini rami in s čajnikom, ki je za njim pel dva tona, ter poslušal, kako se prebuja sosed.

translation_sl.critic_line: Mesto, ki je preživelo tako, da je svojega stvarnika ohranjalo spečega, se je naučilo vprašati, preden je prestopilo: Nel Vasco je eno sobo dokazala s sinovo krivo zarezo in prepihom po katranu, Dorrit Vane je sprejela ljudi z roba, enainšestdesetim, ki so ostali, pa so povedali neznano resnico in jim dovolili, da jih je strah, medtem ko je Illuminara držala kamen in tišino, ne da bi izbirala namesto kogarkoli od njih.
